units.source_text: “离开故乡时，我已经变得厌世了。

en.t: When I left my hometown, I had already become weary of the world.

units.source_text: 那时，人皆不可信的观念已经嵌入了我的骨髓。

en.t: By then, the idea that no one could be trusted had already sunk into my very bones.

units.source_text: 我觉得我所敌视的叔叔、婶婶和其他亲戚，仿佛就是人类的代表，就连坐在火车上，我也有意无意地用这种眼光观察旁边的人。

en.t: I began to feel that the uncle, aunt, and other relatives I hated were somehow representatives of all humanity, and even when I sat on the train, I found myself, half consciously and half unconsciously, observing the people beside me through that same lens.

units.source_text: 有时他们跟我搭话，我就更加戒备了。

en.t: When they sometimes spoke to me, I became even more guarded.

units.source_text: 我的心是阴沉的，常常犹如吞了铅似的沉重不堪。

en.t: My heart was gloomy, and it often felt unbearably heavy, as though I had swallowed lead.

units.source_text: 然而，我的神经却如刚才所说，变得越发敏感了。

en.t: And yet, as I have just said, my nerves grew more and more sensitive.

units.source_text: 到东京后，我想搬出寄宿处，主要也是这个缘故。

en.t: This was also the main reason why, after arriving in Tokyo, I wanted to move out of my lodging house.

units.source_text: 如果说是因为花钱随心所欲，才想自己单找住处，也并非不可，但依着我的性子，即便手里有闲钱，也懒得费这事。

en.t: It would not be wrong to say that I wanted to find a place of my own because I could now spend money as I pleased, but by nature, even if I had money to spare, I would not have cared to go to that trouble.

units.source_text: 我搬到小石川以后，这种紧张的心情也没能得到一点放松。

en.t: Even after I moved to Koishikawa, this tense state of mind did not ease in the slightest.

units.source_text: 我总是心神不宁地窥视四周，连自己都觉得惭愧。

en.t: I was always restlessly peering around me, to the point that I felt ashamed of myself.

units.source_text: 奇怪的是，不停活动的只是我的大脑和眼睛，嘴巴却与之相反，越来越沉默了。

en.t: Strangely, only my mind and my eyes kept constantly moving, while my mouth, quite the opposite, grew more and more silent.

units.source_text: 我每天都不言不语地坐在桌前，像只猫儿似的观察着这个家里的情况。

en.t: Every day I sat silently at my desk, observing the state of the household like a cat.

units.source_text: 我对她们时刻保持着高度警惕，自己都感觉过意不去，我觉得自己就像个不偷东西的小偷，甚至憎恶起自己来。

en.t: I kept such constant and intense watch over them that I felt sorry for it myself; I thought of myself as a thief who stole nothing, and even came to loathe myself.
